parts.title: A year in Canada
parts.instructions: Read the article and choose the best answer for each question.
parts.passage:
When I was fifteen, I spent a school year in Canada, and it was the hardest and the best year of my life. Before I left Spain, I thought my English was quite good. I had always had high marks at school, and I could understand the songs I listened to. Then I arrived at the airport in Vancouver, and a woman at the desk asked me a question that I did not understand at all.

My host family was very patient. They spoke slowly, and they used a lot of gestures. During the first month, I was so tired in the evenings that I fell asleep as soon as I came home. Listening all day to a foreign language is very hard work. I often smiled and nodded without knowing what people had said, and once I agreed to eat something that turned out to be a very hot chilli.

The change came slowly. One morning, I realised that I had been thinking in English for an hour without noticing. A few weeks later, I made my first joke in English, and my host sister laughed. It was one of the proudest moments of my life.

At the end of the year, I could talk to anybody about almost anything. I also had friends from five different countries. I learned that you need to make mistakes if you want to improve. People did not mind when I used the wrong word, and they usually helped me to find the right one. When I came home, I missed Canada so much that I started to write my diary in English, and I still do.

questions.prompt: How did the writer feel about her English before she left?
options: She was worried about her marks.
questions.explanation: She thought her English was quite good because of her high marks and the songs she understood.

options: She could not understand a question.

questions.explanation: She realised one morning that she had been thinking in English for an hour; the joke came a few weeks later.

They are an important part of learning.

questions.explanation: She learned that you need to make mistakes to improve and people helped her.

parts.title: Growing up with two languages
parts.instructions: Choose the sentence that fits each gap. There are three extra sentences.
parts.passage:
Do you know that more than half of the people in the world speak at least two languages? [1] In many countries, children grow up with two or three languages at home, and they move easily from one to the other.

Scientists have studied bilingual children for many years. [2] For example, they can often concentrate better, and they find it easier to learn a third language later.

However, being bilingual is not always simple. Some children mix words from both languages in one sentence, and parents sometimes worry. [3] Teachers say that this is normal, and that it usually stops as the child gets older.

Families who want to raise bilingual children have several options. One common method is that each parent speaks a different language to the child. [4] Others speak one language at home and the other one outside the house.

Whatever method they choose, experts agree on one thing: children need plenty of chances to hear and use both languages. [5] A grandparent who tells stories in the second language can be just as helpful as an expensive school.
sentences: Some families also ask a relative to talk to the child in a different language.
It does not always have to be a formal lesson, as this can be done through games, songs and conversation.
Adults usually find it harder to learn a language than children.
They found that these children often have some advantages at school.
Learning a language is easier with a good dictionary.
In fact, this is a normal stage of learning two languages at the same time.
Being bilingual is normal for a large part of the population.
That is why many children learn to read late.

gaps.explanation: The question about half the world speaking two languages is answered by sentence F: being bilingual is normal; the next sentence is about children growing up with languages.
"Scientists have studied bilingual children" leads to what they found; "For example" gives the advantages.
Parents worry about mixed words; "In fact, this is a normal stage" reassures them, and the next sentence says teachers agree.
One method is each parent using a different language; "Others speak..." in the next sentence is a second method, and sentence A is another option that fits between them.
Children need chances to hear both languages; the next sentence says it does not have to be formal, and the final sentence gives the example of a grandparent.

parts.title: Learning new words
parts.instructions: Choose the correct word for each gap.
parts.passage: Many students believe that the best way to learn vocabulary is to read a long list and try to [1] it by heart. Unfortunately, this method does not usually work. Research shows that we remember words better when we meet them several times in different [2]. One idea is to keep a small notebook. Each time you hear a new word, write it down with an example sentence and a picture. Another helpful idea is to review your notes [3] a day or two, and again after a week. You will then be more [4] to remember the word for a long time. You can also stick small notes with words onto the objects in your room. Every time you look at the door or the window, you will see its name, and the word will gradually become [5] of your memory. Finally, do not be afraid to use new words, even if you [6] a mistake.

questions.prompt: Gap 1
questions.explanation: "Learn it by heart" is the fixed expression.

questions.prompt: Gap 2
questions.explanation: We remember words better when we meet them in different situations.

questions.prompt: Gap 3
questions.explanation: Review the words "after a day or two".

questions.prompt: Gap 4
questions.explanation: "More likely to remember" means there is a better chance of remembering.

questions.prompt: Gap 5
questions.explanation: "Become part of your memory" is the correct phrase.

questions.prompt: Gap 6
questions.explanation: We "make a mistake".

parts.title: An email to a host family
parts.instructions: Write one word in each gap.
parts.passage:
Dear Mr and Mrs Rowe,
Thank you very much for agreeing to have me in your house [1] the summer. I am looking forward to meeting you all. My English is not perfect, [2] I will try to speak as much as I can. I am arriving at the airport on Saturday [3] two o'clock. I will wear a blue jacket, so you [4] recognise me easily. I have never been to England, so I do not know [5] the weather will be like. Should I bring a raincoat? Please tell me if there is anything that I [6] not eat.
Best wishes,
Marta

gaps.explanation: "For the summer" says how long she will stay.
"But" contrasts her imperfect English with her promise to try.
We use "at" with a clock time.
A modal verb says that they will be able to recognise her.
"What the weather will be like" is the correct indirect question.
"Anything I must not eat" refers to foods that she should avoid.

parts.title: Short conversations
parts.instructions: Listen to seven short conversations. Choose the correct answer.

turns.speaker: amadeus
turns.text: Hello Beatrix, this is Amadeus from the language school. I’m calling about your German class. You were told it was on Monday evening, but I’m afraid the room isn’t free any more. Thursday has the open evening for new students, so we can’t use that day either. The only choice is Wednesday, at the same time, half past six, in room twelve. I hope that’s all right with you. If you can’t make it, please send me an email before the weekend and we’ll find another solution. Thank you very much.

question.prompt: Which day is the German class now?
question.explanation: Monday’s room is not free and Thursday is the open evening, so the class moves to Wednesday at half past six.

turns.speaker: celestine
turns.text: Dorian, I’ve started a Portuguese course. Isn’t that great?

turns.speaker: dorian
turns.text: Really? Are you planning to go to Brazil? I remember you talked about a long holiday there.

turns.speaker: celestine
turns.text: Maybe one day, but not yet. I’m not thinking about a new job abroad either, I’m happy at the bank. The truth is that my grandmother moved to Lisbon last year, and she’s lonely. She hardly speaks any English.

turns.speaker: dorian
turns.text: That’s so kind of you.

turns.speaker: celestine
turns.text: I want to phone her every Sunday and chat in her own language.

turns.speaker: dorian
turns.text: She’ll be delighted.

question.prompt: Why is the girl learning Portuguese?
options: For a long holiday in Brazil
To get a much better job abroad
question.explanation: The holiday and the job abroad are not her plans; her grandmother lives in Lisbon and speaks little English, so she wants to chat with her in Portuguese.

turns.speaker: evander2
turns.text: Hello, Felicia. Are you interested in the Italian course for beginners?

turns.speaker: felicity
turns.text: Yes. How much is it, roughly? My friend told me it was about twenty-five.

turns.speaker: evander2
turns.text: That’s the price of the intermediate one. The beginners’ course is less, around twenty pounds for the term, with the book included.

turns.speaker: felicity
turns.text: That’s cheaper than I expected. Last year I paid fifteen pounds for a short Spanish workshop, and it was only two evenings.

turns.speaker: evander2
turns.text: Then this is much better value. Shall I put your name down?

turns.speaker: felicity
turns.text: Yes, please.

question.prompt: How much will the woman pay, roughly?
question.explanation: Twenty-five is the intermediate course and fifteen was her Spanish workshop, so the beginners’ course costs about twenty pounds.

turns.speaker: gaspard
turns.text: Henriette, do you like your new French teacher?

turns.speaker: henriette
turns.text: I do. Some people say that she’s strict, but that was Mr Hall, last year, and he never smiled. And we don’t have an easy time with homework either, there’s a lot of it.

turns.speaker: gaspard
turns.text: So what’s good about her?

turns.speaker: henriette
turns.text: She spent ten years in Senegal, and she tells us stories about the markets and the food and the music. We learn words without even noticing.

turns.speaker: gaspard
turns.text: That sounds much better than my class.

turns.speaker: henriette
turns.text: You should ask to change.

question.prompt: What does the boy like about his teacher?
options: She gives students very little homework.
She tells stories about a country.
She is very strict with all the students.
question.explanation: Mr Hall was the strict one and the homework is heavy, but she likes the teacher because she tells stories about her years in Senegal.

turns.speaker: ignacio
turns.text: Okay, everybody, before you leave, a word about homework. Last week you wrote a story about your holidays, and I enjoyed reading them, so there’s no need for another one. Some of you asked if you can read a whole book for next time, which is a lovely idea, but let’s wait until the holidays. For tomorrow, please do exercise four on page twenty-two. It’s about the past simple and should take about twenty minutes. Don’t leave it for the morning bus! If you have any questions, please ask me now. Otherwise, have a good evening.

question.prompt: What must the students do for homework?
question.explanation: The story was last week and the book can wait for the holidays; for tomorrow they must do exercise four.

turns.speaker: kasimir
turns.text: Hi everyone, this is Kasimir with the dates for the exams. Please write them down. The written paper is on the twelfth of June, in the big hall, and you’ll get your results on the nineteenth. The speaking test is a different day and a different room. It’s earlier, on the fifth of June, so you have less than two weeks to practise with your partner. I know it seems soon, but the examiners are only free that morning. Please arrive fifteen minutes early and bring your identity card. Good luck!

question.explanation: The written paper is on the twelfth and the results on the nineteenth, but the speaking test is earlier, on the fifth.

turns.speaker: leopoldo
turns.text: Marianne, you’re coming to the cooking class in Spanish tomorrow, aren’t you? What do I need to bring?

turns.speaker: marianne
turns.text: I thought of taking my laptop, to look up words.

turns.speaker: leopoldo
turns.text: There’s no need, the teacher says phones aren’t allowed in the kitchen. A big dictionary would be too heavy, and there are some on the shelf anyway.

turns.speaker: marianne
turns.text: So what will I use?

turns.speaker: leopoldo
turns.text: A small book for new words, and something to write with. That’s all.

turns.speaker: marianne
turns.text: Easy. I’ll put them in my apron pocket.

question.prompt: What should the woman take to the class?
options: A big dictionary and a bag
question.explanation: Computers are not allowed, a big dictionary is heavy and the school has them, so she only needs a small notebook and a pen.

parts.title: Understanding the main idea
parts.instructions: Listen to six short conversations and choose the best answer.

turns.speaker: nathaniel
turns.text: Odalie, I’m so worried about the English test on Friday.

turns.speaker: ottoline2
turns.text: But you’re always top of the class. You do your homework and you read novels in English.

turns.speaker: nathaniel
turns.text: Yes, I know, the writing and the reading are fine. It’s the speaking part. When the teacher looks at me and waits, my mind goes blank and my heart beats very fast.

turns.speaker: ottoline2
turns.text: Practise with me after school. I’ll pretend to be the examiner.

turns.speaker: nathaniel
turns.text: Thanks. That might help me relax.

options: He often forgets to do his homework.
He cannot read English very well.
question.explanation: Homework and reading are fine; he becomes nervous and his mind goes blank when he has to talk to the teacher.

turns.speaker: prosper
turns.text: Querida, you look sad. Did you get your exam results?

turns.speaker: querida
turns.text: Yes, and I failed again. I’ve studied for months. I think I should stop the lessons for a while, or just do the exam again in April.

turns.speaker: prosper
turns.text: I wouldn’t give up, and I wouldn’t repeat the same thing. You always learn from your textbook. Why not try films, songs, and chatting with people online? You might remember much more.

turns.speaker: querida
turns.text: That’s an idea. It’s more fun, too.

turns.speaker: prosper
turns.text: Exactly. It’s about learning in a different way.

options: Taking another exam in the spring
Stopping all the lessons for now
question.explanation: She wants to stop or take the exam in April, but he says that studying the same way is the issue and suggests films, songs and chatting.

turns.speaker: rutherford
turns.text: Excuse me, you look lost. Can I help?

turns.speaker: seraphine
turns.text: Yes, please. I want to learn Italian for my trip, so I’d like to buy some books to start. Is there a bookshop near here?

turns.speaker: rutherford
turns.text: There’s one on Mill Street, with a big section for languages. The post office is next door, if you need it.

turns.speaker: seraphine
turns.text: I have to send a parcel, but that can wait. And I’m thinking of joining a school, though I don’t know if I’ll have time. The books come first.

turns.speaker: rutherford
turns.text: Then turn left at the bank and it’s the second shop.

turns.speaker: seraphine
turns.text: Thank you very much.

question.prompt: What does the woman decide to do first?
question.explanation: The post office can wait and the school is only an idea; she says the books come first.

turns.speaker: thelonius
turns.text: Ulrike, I’ve been using a new website to learn Japanese. You should try it.

turns.speaker: ulrike
turns.text: Is it expensive? The last one was thirty pounds a month.

turns.speaker: thelonius
turns.text: Not at all. There are no payments, no advertisements, nothing. A group of students makes it as a hobby. There aren’t any teachers or certificates, but I don’t need them. I just want to talk to my friends in Tokyo.

turns.speaker: ulrike
turns.text: Hmm, if it’s free, then why not?

turns.speaker: thelonius
turns.text: I’ll send you the link tonight.

question.prompt: What does the man like about the website?
question.explanation: The other website was expensive; he says there are no payments, and he does not need teachers or a certificate.

turns.speaker: valerian
turns.text: Wilhelmine, you’ve got your exam result. What did you get?

turns.speaker: wilhelmine
turns.text: Eighty-five per cent! I can’t believe it. Last year I failed, and I almost gave up Spanish.

turns.speaker: valerian
turns.text: Congratulations! Were you expecting a better mark?

turns.speaker: wilhelmine
turns.text: Not at all. I only wanted to pass. And the questions weren’t confusing at all, I knew what to write. I worked so hard, and now I’ve done it by myself. I’ll tell my parents tonight with a big smile.

turns.speaker: valerian
turns.text: You deserve it.

question.explanation: She only wanted to pass and the questions were clear; she worked hard and is happy about what she achieved by herself.

turns.speaker: xiomara
turns.text: Yannick, why are you hiding behind your book? Are you late again?

turns.speaker: yannick
turns.text: No, I was on time today. And my dictionary is in my bag, I checked twice.

turns.speaker: xiomara
turns.text: So what’s the matter?

turns.speaker: yannick
turns.text: In the lesson, I wanted to say that I was hot, and I said I was a hot person, you know, in a different sense. Everyone laughed, even the teacher. My face is still red.

turns.speaker: xiomara
turns.text: Oh, that’s a classic mistake! Don’t worry, everybody makes them.

turns.speaker: yannick
turns.text: I hope they forget it soon.

options: He was late for class again.
He lost his dictionary on the bus.
He made a silly mistake in front of everyone.
question.explanation: He was on time and still has his dictionary; what embarrasses him is the mistake that made the whole class laugh.

parts.title: A talk at a language school open day
parts.instructions: Listen to the talk and complete each note. Write one or two words, a number, a date or a time.

turns.speaker: speaker-1
turns.text: Good afternoon, and welcome to the Greenfield Language School. I’m Cornelius, the director. First, a few facts about us. We offer courses in six languages: English, Spanish, French, German, Italian and Japanese. We wanted to add Chinese this year, but we couldn’t find a teacher, so perhaps next year. Our classes are small. In many schools there are twenty people in a room, but here the maximum is eight students, so every person speaks a lot. Now, the timetable. There are morning and evening lessons. The morning ones finish at midday. In the evening, the classes start at half past six, and we have to stop at nine o’clock, because the building closes. I know that some of you would like to stay later, but the neighbours complain. Next, the length of the course. Our short courses last four weeks, and our summer intensive ones are only two, but the standard one lasts ten weeks, and it’s the one that most students choose. At the end, there’s an exam and a certificate. Let me also tell you about the library. It’s on the first floor and it’s open every day. You are welcome to borrow books and films, so that you can enjoy the language at home. You can’t take out magazines, but you can read them there. We don’t sell textbooks in the library, they are in the shop downstairs. And now my favourite part. Today is a special day. If you register before six o’clock, you’ll receive a free dictionary. I’d love to say a free course, but that’s not possible. The dictionary is a good one, and it normally costs eighteen pounds. Please come to the desk by the door, and my colleagues will help you. Thank you for your attention, and I hope you’ll join us!

gaps.prompt: The school offers lessons in ___ different languages
gaps.explanation: They wanted to add Chinese but could not find a teacher, so there are six.

gaps.prompt: Nobody sits in a larger group than ___ students
gaps.explanation: Many schools have twenty, but here the maximum is eight.

gaps.prompt: The building closes, so evening lessons stop at ___ o'clock
gaps.explanation: Evening classes start at half past six and stop at nine; morning classes finish at midday.

gaps.prompt: The most common course takes ___ weeks
gaps.explanation: Short courses last four weeks and intensive ones two, but the standard one lasts ten.

gaps.prompt: Members can take home books and ___ from the library
gaps.explanation: They can borrow books and films, not magazines.

gaps.prompt: Anyone who signs up before six o'clock receives a ___ as a gift
gaps.explanation: A free course is not possible; the gift is a dictionary.

parts.title: An interview with a Spanish teacher
parts.instructions: Listen to the interview and choose the correct answer.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Augustina, you teach Spanish. What first made you interested in languages?

turns.speaker: augustina
turns.text: People assume that I grew up speaking two languages, but no, my family only spoke English. And I did work in a bank abroad, but that came much later. It started when I found a box of old letters in my grandmother’s house. They were written in Spanish and I wanted to know what was inside. I spent a whole summer with a dictionary, and I was hooked.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: In your opinion, what makes a good teacher?

turns.speaker: augustina
turns.text: It isn’t about knowing the most words. I’ve met teachers with huge vocabularies who couldn’t explain anything. And speaking fast isn’t a gift, believe me. A good teacher helps two people understand each other, with their different cultures and ideas. That’s the real job, and that is what I enjoy.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: What do you find difficult?

turns.speaker: augustina
turns.text: There’s never a problem with classrooms, we have plenty, and marking homework is a pleasure for me, I like seeing the progress. What is hard is being patient with shy students. Some of them hardly speak for weeks, and I have to wait, smile and not push too hard. It tests me every day.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Have you ever made a mistake in class?

turns.speaker: augustina
turns.text: Several, but one stays in my memory. Once I mixed up the names of two students, but that was just embarrassing. And I have never missed a lesson in my life. No, the worst was a word I wrote wrongly on the board. I meant to write, you are a fine student, and instead I wrote something rude. The class laughed for ten minutes.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Will computers replace teachers?

turns.speaker: augustina
turns.text: Programs are impressive, but I don’t think they are nearly as good as a person. They can’t understand a joke, or hear that you’re sad. They are not too expensive either, many are free, so it’s not about money. It’s about feelings, and machines don’t have any.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: What would you tell young people who want to learn a language?

turns.speaker: augustina
turns.text: Go and live where people speak it, even for a few months. Of course, you should study grammar, but not every day, and you don’t have to become a teacher. If you listen to the people in the street and the shop, you learn faster than in any classroom.

questions.prompt: How did Augustina become interested in languages?
options: She grew up in a bilingual family.
She wanted to read old letters.
She worked in a bank abroad.
questions.explanation: Her family spoke only English and the bank was later; she found old letters in Spanish and wanted to read them.

questions.prompt: What does she think makes a good teacher?
options: Helping people to understand each other
questions.explanation: A big vocabulary and speed are not important; a good teacher helps two people understand each other.

questions.prompt: What does she find most difficult in her job?
questions.explanation: Classrooms are not a problem and she likes marking; what is hard is waiting for shy students.

questions.prompt: What mistake did she make once?
options: She forgot to attend a lesson.
She wrote a wrong word on the board.
questions.explanation: Mixing up names was only embarrassing and she never missed a lesson; the worst was the rude word she wrote on the board.

questions.prompt: What does she say about computers?
options: They are almost as good as people now.
They cannot understand jokes or feelings.
They are far too expensive for most people.
questions.explanation: They are not too expensive and they are not nearly as good as people; they cannot understand a joke or hear that someone is sad.

questions.prompt: What does she advise young people to do?
questions.explanation: She says to live where people speak it; grammar every day and teaching are not necessary.
